source_evidence: Variable annuities are tax-deferred. That means you pay no federal taxes on the income and investment gains from your annuity until you make a withdrawal, receive income payments, or a death benefit is paid.
answer: Tax deferral means federal taxes on a variable annuity’s income and investment gains are postponed until you withdraw money, receive annuity payments, or a death benefit is paid. When you withdraw money or receive annuitized payments, gains are taxed at ordinary federal income tax rates rather than lower capital gains rates. Tax deferral is not the same as tax-free growth. The source also notes that a variable annuity held within an IRA or 401(k) provides no additional tax advantage, and that tax rules can be complicated and may change.
